signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia (market context for AikBank)
signals.signal: NBS acceptance-network TRANSACTION statistics, updated 19/08/2026, split ATM activity into cash-in and cash-out for the first time in this reporting window. For cards issued by Serbian payment service providers: Q2-2026 ATM DEPOSITS (uplata) 3,406,129 transactions worth RSD 173,936m; Q2-2026 ATM WITHDRAWALS (isplata) 27,288,350 transactions worth RSD 552,239m. Q1-2026 comparatives: deposits 3,202,644 / RSD 151,638m; withdrawals 24,793,602 / RSD 493,997m. So ATM cash-in grew 6.4% q/q by count and 14.7% q/q by value, faster than cash-out (+10.1% by count, +11.8% by value). Deposits are 11.1% of ATM transaction count but 24.0% of ATM transaction value. Cards not issued in Serbia recorded ZERO ATM deposit transactions in both quarters.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Serbia - payment system statistics, 'Transakcije na prihvatnoj mrezi' XLSX, sheet 2026-srp/2026-eng
signals.implies: This is the quantified demand case to put in front of AikBank. Deposit traffic at Serbian ATMs is growing faster than withdrawal traffic and already carries a quarter of all ATM value, while 457 of AikBank's 570 machines physically cannot take a deposit. Every deposit transaction the bank cannot serve at a machine either goes to a branch counter - which AikBank is actively shortening cash-desk hours to avoid - or to a competitor's machine. Direct, numerate justification for a recycler / deposit-ATM upgrade programme.
signals.followup: Build the per-machine economics: RSD 173.9bn of quarterly ATM cash-in across 3,412 machines, against AikBank's 16.7% ATM share and its 20% deposit-capable ratio, to size the value AikBank is currently forgoing.

signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia (regulatory clock on AikBank)
signals.signal: PRIMARY TEXT READ IN FULL (21-page official PDF). The NBS Decision on video identification, Executive Board no. 14 of 07/05/2026, published in Official Gazette RS 43/2026, sets these transitional rules. Point 36: it enters into force on the eighth day after publication. Point 33: obligors already performing video identification under the old 2019/2020/2021 decision must align their business and internal acts within SIX MONTHS of entry into force, and must adapt their TECHNICAL SOLUTIONS, where necessary, within ONE YEAR of entry into force. Point 30: any obligor intending to offer video identification must notify NBS at least 30 DAYS before starting, submitting internal acts, proof of staff training and further documentation - and under point 31 must give NBS staff a live, real-time DEMONSTRATION of the entire process for every category of customer before that deadline expires. The decision also creates a route for 'posredna video-identifikacija' (indirect video identification), where supervision and verification of the performing employee happens before the relationship is established or, exceptionally, within 72 hours afterwards under enhanced monitoring and transaction limits. Point 35 repeals the 2019 decision outright.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Serbia - Odluka o video-identifikaciji, Sl. glasnik RS 43/2026 (official PDF, text extracted with pdfminer)
signals.implies: The best-timed compliance play in Serbia, and AikBank is the sharpest case for it: its online account opening (launched 08/04/2026) depends on a STAFFED video call restricted to weekdays 08:00-20:00 and Saturdays 08:00-19:00. The new 'indirect video identification' route is precisely what removes that staffing constraint and enables 24/7 straight-through onboarding, while the prescriptive technical standard plus the mandatory live demonstration to NBS is the kind of requirement banks buy rather than build. Sell Printec digital onboarding/eKYC with the AML/compliance suite behind it as a compliance-by-design package, mapped clause by clause - at AikBank first, then across the market.
signals.likelihood: Certain in force; every Serbian bank offering video ID must comply
signals.followup: CONFIRM THE EXACT DEADLINES: the decision dates the deadlines from entry into force, which is eight days after publication in Gazette 43/2026. The NBS filename encodes 20260519; if the Gazette date is 19/05/2026 then entry into force is 27/05/2026, the conduct deadline is around 27/11/2026 and the technical-solution deadline around 27/05/2027. Verify the Gazette publication date at pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs before quoting these dates to a client - they are derived, not stated in the decision.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run - no checkpoint existed for 2026-08-27. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200 calls) before a single AikBank query could be issued, so open-web keyword discovery was impossible. The entire run was therefore executed primary-source-first by direct HTTP fetching with a desktop User-Agent, which the brief prefers anyway. Angles worked: (1) AikBank's own machine-readable locator feed and news-index feed (/vesti/vesti.json), giving a complete dated inventory of 2026 branch and ATM activity; (2) AikBank's audited FY2025 filings index, from which the previously-uncited GROUP-level ('bankarska grupa') consolidated accounts were pulled and read - a source the baseline never opened; (3) the Serbian regulator, using the NBS payment-system statistics XLSX files rather than press summaries, which yielded Q2-2026 acceptance-network AND transaction-level data refreshed 19/08/2026; (4) the Serbian official-journal text of the NBS video-identification decision, read in full for the first time rather than summarised; (5) the Zagreb Stock Exchange EHO issuer register, searched by ticker, to verify the Croatian deal status at the exchange rather than at the issuer's website alone; (6) the OTHER AikGroup banks' own locator infrastructure - Hipotekarna banka (Montenegro) and Gorenjska banka (Slovenia) - which the baseline had only ever cited second-hand through AikBank marketing copy. GROUP FLEET RECONCILIATION was completed as the brief requested: Serbia 570 + Montenegro 49 + Slovenia 64 = approximately 683 ATMs from three independent operator sources. THE MOST IMPORTANT NEW FINDING is competitive rather than technical: AikBank's own August customer notices route customers to MoneyGet, an independent ATM deployer operated by Payten d.o.o. / Asseco South Eastern Europe - a direct Printec competitor - which lists 200 ATM sites in Serbia and operates in three of AikGroup's four markets. GENUINE GAPS: AikBank publishes no interim (H1/Q2) financial statements at all, only audited annuals, so the August reporting-cluster angle produced nothing for this bank and the freshest financials remain FY2025; there is no published AikBank ATM/POS terminal count and no published refresh schedule; no NCR Atleos or other ATM-vendor incumbency for AikBank could be established from primary sources (the NCR Atleos sitemap contains no Serbia or AikBank page), so the 'NCR Atleos win' element of the brief is UNCONFIRMED and is deliberately not reported as a signal rather than being sourced to an aggregator; the Hipotekarna JSON carries no deposit/recycler flag so Montenegro's cash-in capability is unmeasured; and AikGroup's own corporate domain (aikgroup.eu) did not resolve.
access_issues: 1) WebSearch was unavailable for the whole run - the session budget of 200 calls was consumed before this task began. All findings are direct fetches; no aggregator was used and none is cited. 2) aikbank.rs serves its financial-statement PDFs GZIP-ENCODED without transparent decompression, so they sniff as 'gzip compressed data' and pdfminer rejects them with 'No /Root object'; they must be gunzipped first. Logged and worked around. 3) hipotekarnabanka.com/filijale-i-bankomati/ is fully JavaScript-rendered and returns only a 'Ucitavanje...' placeholder to a fetch. Per the escalation rules I did NOT drop to press: I read the locator plugin source at wp-content/plugins/hbforms1.11.2/business-locations/locations.js, recovered the AJAX action name, and called POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with action=hb_business_locations_list, which returns 41KB of clean JSON. Browser escalation was not needed. 4) Two NBS URLs 404'd on first guess (nbs.rs/sr_RS/finansijske-institucije/platni-sistem/statistika/ and /sr/finansijske-institucije/platni-promet/statistika/); the working path was found from the NBS homepage link graph at /sr/ciljevi-i-funkcije/platni-sistem/statistika/. Logged. 5) eho.zse.hr/pretraga?izdavatelj=... 404s; the working search is /obavijesti-izdavatelja/search with the tx_issuerpublicationmanager_publicnewslisting[query] and [filter]=ticker parameters, read from the page's own form markup. 6) https://www.aikgroup.eu/ failed to connect (curl exit 6, no DNS resolution) - the group holding company has no reachable public site, which is why all group-level facts here are triangulated from the subsidiaries' own filings and locators. 7) gbkr.si exposes no WP REST API (wp-json 404s; the site remaps it to /gbkr-api/), so the Slovenian count was taken from branch-sitemap.xml plus per-page title checks instead.
operator_requests: None blocking - notably, the standing operator request for a machine-readable Hipotekarna banka (Montenegro) fleet count is now CLOSED by this run via the admin-ajax endpoint documented above. Two items would benefit from an operator with a raised WebSearch/browse budget rather than a paywall bypass: (a) confirm the Official Gazette RS 43/2026 PUBLICATION DATE at pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs, so the six-month and twelve-month video-identification deadlines can be stated as facts rather than derived from the NBS filename; (b) test whether any primary source supports the 'NCR Atleos win' premise in the brief for AikBank or AikGroup - nothing on ncratleos.com references Serbia or AikBank, and I declined to source it to an aggregator. No paywalled or gated PDF was encountered in this run.
